packageRules.description: Our own packages skip the release-age wait. `minimumReleaseAge` above holds every third-party release back a week, so a compromised one has time to be yanked before Renovate proposes it -- and `:automergeMinor` would otherwise merge it unreviewed. Releases made in Jebel-Quant are not that risk, and the companion-package flow is release-then-bump: a new setting or check lands in the package, then rhiza moves its pin to use it. A week's wait there only delays the bump. Security updates bypass the wait regardless (Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts default). tests/api/test_supply_chain_pins.py holds both lists.

The `python` base image in `bundles/docker/docker/Dockerfile` is `python:${PYTHON_VERSION}-slim`, and `ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.12` is only a fallback. Every real build passes `--build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=$(cat .python-version)`, so `.python-version` is the single source of truth, as the Dockerfile's own header says. Renovate reads the fallback as the image tag and proposes bumping it (3.12 -> 3.15), which would make the fallback disagree with `.python-version` here and in python-core while changing nothing a build uses. Moving Python is a `.python-version` decision, not an image bump. Only the `python` image is disabled: the uv builder image's `-python3.12-` part is a tag suffix Renovate keeps as-is, so uv updates still arrive.

customManagers.description: The pytest-rhiza pin in `[tool.rhiza-task]`. `make rhiza-test` installs the rhiza repository checks at an exact version so the checks and the template move as one number (#1540). No built-in manager reads that table -- pep621 sees only the dependency arrays -- so without this the pin only ages. It targeted `RHIZA_CHECKS_VERSION` in `.rhiza/make.d/quality.mk` until #1579, and went silently dead when that file retired -- #1556 for this repo, #1557 for the bundle: a manager whose file pattern matches nothing reports no error, it just stops finding updates.

The `RHIZA_TASK` pin: `bundles/core/Makefile` names the CLI that runs every gate, and the six live `.github/workflows/` plus the five GitLab bundle stubs repeat it because a reusable workflow cannot read a consumer's variable. Thirteen literals, one dependency -- Renovate groups by dep+version, so they move in one PR, which is the property that matters: a partial bump leaves the shim and the workflows disagreeing about which CLI runs the gates. Without this manager the pin only ages, exactly as the pytest-rhiza one did (#1579): it sat at 0.3.1 while upstream shipped 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, and #1580 had to move all eleven by hand. This entry lives in the *root* renovate.json only, which is an intentional mother-repo override (utils/link_dogfood.py's exclusion list). Shipping it in `bundles/renovate/` would put it in consumers, where it would bump a template-owned file that the next `/rhiza:update` overwrites -- a PR loop, not an update. The bundle GitLab stubs, and the GitHub release workflow the `github` bundle ships whole (it cannot be a stub -- PyPI Trusted Publishing validates the calling file), are in scope here because they are authored in this repo, which is where a consumer's copy gets its value. The root `Makefile` is deliberately NOT matched: it is a dogfood symlink into bundles/core/, and writing through that path would replace the link with a regular file. tests/api/test_renovate_managers.py holds every one of these claims.

The tectonic pin the paper and book workflows install (the book needs it because `paper` is a prerequisite of `book`, and a skipped prerequisite publishes a nav entry with no asset behind it). tectonic is the LaTeX engine rhiza-task's `paper` task drives, and neither pipeline can assume a runner has it -- so each downloads a pinned release asset. The file patterns are the whole workflow folders rather than the two filenames, so a third caller is watched the day it is added rather than the day somebody notices. No built-in manager reads a `TECTONIC_VERSION` variable, and an unmanaged pin only ages, which is the lesson of #1579 (the pytest-rhiza manager) and #1582 (RHIZA_TASK, which had no manager at all). Upstream tags releases `tectonic@X.Y.Z`, hence extractVersionTemplate; the workflows re-encode the `@` for the download URL. The asset is deliberately not checksum-verified: nothing can keep a digest in step with an automated bump, so a pinned digest would turn each of these PRs into a red paper build in every consumer.

The `UV_VERSION` pin in `bundles/core/Makefile`: the uv the shim's bootstrap installs (`astral.sh/uv/$(UV_VERSION)/install.sh`) on a runner with no uv on PATH. Before #1797 the URL was unversioned, so a fresh runner got whatever uv astral released last -- the one unpinned step in a toolchain that pins everything else, inherited by every consumer. Root renovate.json only, for the same reason as the RHIZA_TASK manager: in a consumer the shim is template-owned and the next sync would overwrite the bump. The root `Makefile` is not matched because it is the dogfood symlink. The same manager also owns every `astral-sh/setup-uv` `version:` in the live and bundled GitHub workflows and the GitLab `UV_IMAGE` tag (#1818): with only the shim watched, the shim moved to 0.13.x while CI and every GitLab consumer sat on 0.11.16 -- the drift #1383 had already fixed once. One manager, one dep name, so Renovate moves them in one PR. The Dockerfile builder image is the dockerfile manager's, and the uv-pre-commit hook is a separate dependency, so both arrive as separate PRs. tests/api/test_renovate_managers.py holds these claims.
